packets.responsibility: Section header (2131-2136, 6 lines): states the module-level SINGLETON design — COMP_VIEW/SELF_KEYS/SELF_VIEW are built ONCE at script-load time and their accessors read `_ectx`/`state` at the moment an expression touches them, not per-evaluation objects; this keeps the hot compiled-expression path allocation-free, and the two genuinely expensive operations (resolving which layer a per-shape holder belongs to; building a marker list) run only when an expression actually reads a field that needs them. resolveHolderLayer(holder) (2137-2146): an exact-match scan of `state.layers` for a LAYER holder (returns {ld:holder, index, strokeId:null} immediately), else a scan of every layer's own `elementMotion` map for an ELEMENT holder (value-identity match via `em[k]===holder`, returns {ld, index, strokeId:k}); returns null if holder is neither. See boundaries for why this is exactly TWO branches, not three, despite mesh holders reusing the second one. Lead-in (2147-2148, 2 lines): the scan is O(layers x shapes) and several `self` fields want the identical answer within one evaluation. _selfResolved() (2149-2154): memoizes resolveHolderLayer(ctx.holder) onto `ctx._resolved` (undefined check, not truthy check — so a real `null` result, e.g. a stray/detached holder, is cached too and never re-scanned within the same evaluation) — the cache key IS the ephemeral per-evaluation `_ectx` object itself (C20m, motion.js:2563-2569), so it never survives past one compiled-function call. _selfLd() (2155, one line): `r ? r.ld : null` — the layer object regardless of holder kind. COMP_VIEW (2156-2170): width/height read state.canvasW/canvasH directly; fps delegates to _exprFps() (pre-C20k, motion.js:1371, itself `state.fps || 24`); frames/layers read state.totalFrames/state.layers.length; name (2162-2169, the only multi-line getter) returns the ACTIVE COMPONENT's own name when `state.activeSymbolId` names a live entry in `state.symbols`, else the literal string 'Scene' — so an expression's `comp.name` reflects whichever Component the user is currently editing INSIDE (CLAUDE.md §8's Component-scoped editing), not always the top-level project; marker delegates to _markerApi(state.markers) (C20k.markers, motion.js:2107), the project-level marker list. SELF_KEYS (2171-2176): 'self.keys — the current property's own keyframes' (2171); at(i) floors i and calls exprKeyAt(c.holder, c.prop, ...) (C20k, motion.js:2064); nearest(f) calls exprNearestKeyAtFrame(c.holder, c.prop, f) (C20k, motion.js:2091) with f taken as FRAMES, no conversion; count is an ES5 getter calling exprNumKeys(c.holder, c.prop) (C20k, motion.js:2070) LIVE on every read — unlike packet 3's own `numKeys` alias, which is evaluated once and bound as a plain number (see boundaries). All three silently return null/0 if `_ectx` is absent (an accessor read outside any expression evaluation, which cannot normally happen but is guarded anyway). SELF_VIEW (2177-2183): the base object literal — at/velocity/speed/control are bare references to exprSelfAt/exprSelfVelocity/exprSelfSpeed/exprSelfControl (C20k, motion.js:1823/1834/1844/2020), keys is the SELF_KEYS object just built. Packet 2 (2184-2249) adds fourteen more properties to this SAME object via Object.defineProperty after it is constructed — SELF_VIEW is one object, built in two packets.

packets.responsibility: Section header + narrative comment (2184-2196, 13 lines, 2026-08-30): image meshes became animatable per vertex (CLAUDE.md §12ter), but an expression had no way to know WHICH vertex it was running on, so animating a whole mesh surface by hand meant keying every vertex individually (75 tracks for a 10-column mesh); with the vertex index and its own REST position available, one expression (`var uv = self.vertexUV; [0, Math.sin(uv[0]*6+time*3)*8]`) describes the whole surface. The comment is explicit that vertexUV is the REST position (normalized 0..1 over the image), never the POSED one, because an expression reading its own output would feed back on itself frame after frame. _selfMesh() (2197-2201): returns null unless `_selfResolved()` yields a holder with a non-null strokeId AND `window.SMImageMesh` exists, else `SMImageMesh.get(r.strokeId) || null` (image-mesh.js:73) — here `r.strokeId` is read as if it MIGHT be a meshId, which is exactly the reuse boundaries documents: resolveHolderLayer never knows or cares that the string is a meshId, only SMImageMesh.get's own lookup determines that. _selfVertexIndex() (2202-2207): reads `_ectx.prop`, matches it against `/^vtx(\d+)$/`, returns the captured integer or -1 — this is the SAME `vtxN` naming convention CLAUDE.md §12ter documents for per-vertex motion tracks. The fourteen SELF_VIEW getters added here (2208-2249) fall into four groups: (a) mesh identity — isMesh (2208, `!!_selfMesh()`), vertexIndex (2209, a direct getter alias of _selfVertexIndex), vertexCount (2210-2212, `m.verts.length` or 0), vertexUV (2213-2219, `[m.verts[i][0], m.verts[i][1]]` or `[0,0]` — the RAW 0..1 rest-position pair, a DIFFERENT unit from the per-vertex ANIMATION offset elsewhere in the app, which CLAUDE.md §12ter documents as stored in PERCENT (0-100) of image size), isOutlineVertex (2220-2225, `i < m.outline.length` — true only for the contour/mask vertices CLAUDE.md §12 describes as square orange handles in the editor); (b) generic holder identity, unrelated to mesh — property (2226, bare `_ectx.prop`), name (2227, `_selfLd().name`), index (2228, `_selfResolved().index`); (c) the mesh-vs-shape disambiguation — a 3-line comment (2229-2231) states a mesh holder used to answer `isShape:true` (it is 'keyed like an element holder' — same map, see boundaries), which made `self.isShape` useless once meshes and shapes could both be present; isShape (2232) is now `!!(r && r.strokeId != null) && !_selfMesh()` — true only for an ACTUAL per-shape element holder; (d) layer-context passthroughs — inPoint/outPoint (2233-2238, delegate to window.layerInPoint/layerOutPoint, app.js:2838/2889, guarded by existence, default 0 / state.totalFrames-1), hasParent (2239, `!!ld.parentLayerUid`), parent (2240-2248, resolves the parent layer's UID via findLayerIndexByUid — motion.js:3564, sibling-covered — and returns a full layerSnapshot, C20k.other-layers, motion.js:1957, AT THE CURRENTLY-EVALUATING frame, `_ectx.frame`), marker (2249, `_markerApi(ld.markers)` — this LAYER's own markers, distinct from COMP_VIEW.marker's project-level list). Lead-in (2251-2256, 6 lines): frames exprContentBox's own SCOPE honestly — Paper.js only materializes geometry for the CURRENTLY LOADED frame, so this always reports the box of whichever frame is being evaluated, 'stated rather than faked'. exprContentBox() (2257-2271): resolves the holder; for a per-shape element holder with a live Paper item, calls liveItemByStrokeId(r.index, r.strokeId) (declared later in the SAME file at motion.js:9732, guarded by `typeof liveItemByStrokeId === 'function'` — a defensive check that is effectively always true once the enclosing IIFE has finished executing, since function declarations hoist regardless of their own source-order position) and reads its `.bounds`; otherwise falls back to the WHOLE layer's own Paper.js layer bounds (`userLayers[r.index].bounds`, app.js:365 global); returns an all-zero box shape if neither resolves; otherwise returns `{x,y,width,height,top,left}` with top/left DUPLICATING y/x on purpose (2268-2269 comment) so the AE-alias `sourceRectAtTime` (packet 3) needs no separate implementation.

signatures: function aliasValueAtTime(t) -> same shape as self.at()
function aliasVelocityAtTime(t) -> same shape as self.velocity()
packets.responsibility: Section header (2273-2279, 7 lines): 'Undocumented on purpose' — these exist for ONE reason, so a snippet pasted from another application doesn't strand the person who pasted it; absent from the help tooltip, the examples menu and every user-facing string, unlike Nemo's own documented vocabulary (EXPR_PUBLIC_NAMES, C20m, motion.js:2360-2376). Where an alias speaks SECONDS and the Nemo primary speaks FRAMES, the conversion happens HERE — 'a silent factor-of-fps error would be nasty'. aliasPosterizeTime(samplesPerSecond) (2280-2286): converts a samples-per-second rate to a frame interval (`ctx.fps / s`) and calls exprStepTime (pre-C20k, motion.js:1709) with it, which snaps the SHARED ephemeral `_ectx.frame`/`_ectx.time` in place — every later call in the SAME expression evaluation that reads the clock then sees the stepped value; returns `ctx.time` in SECONDS 'as the original does'. aliasValueAtTime/aliasVelocityAtTime/aliasSpeedAtTime (2287-2289, one line each): each multiplies its own `t` argument by `c.fps` (or `_exprFps()` if no live `_ectx`) and forwards to exprSelfAt/exprSelfVelocity/exprSelfSpeed (C20k.self-sampling). aliasNearestKey(t) (2290-2293): same seconds-to-frames conversion, forwards to exprNearestKeyAtFrame (C20k). aliasKey(i) (2294, one line): NO conversion — `i` is already a plain keyframe INDEX, forwards to exprKeyAt (C20k) after `Math.floor`. aliasSeedRandom(seed,timeless) (2295-2299): calls exprSeed(seed) (pre-C20k, motion.js:1733) then sets `ctx.rngTimeless = !!timeless` directly on the shared ephemeral context — the second of this scope's own two total mutations (see boundaries). aliasTimeToFrames(t,fps)/aliasFramesToTime(f,fps) (2300-2310): both accept EITHER argument as `undefined` and fall back to the live `_ectx`'s own time/frame/fps in that case, otherwise coerce with `_num`; framesToTime additionally guards `r===0` to avoid a divide-by-zero. resolveHolderLayer does NOT structurally distinguish three holder kinds the issue's own prompt names ('layer ld, element holder ld.elementMotion[strokeId], mesh holder keyed by meshId') — it has exactly TWO branches: an exact match against `state.layers` (a layer holder, strokeId:null), and a scan of every layer's own `elementMotion` map for a value-identity match (an element holder, strokeId:<map key>). A 'mesh holder' is NOT a third branch: it is the identical second branch where the map key happens to be a meshId string instead of a per-shape strokeId string — confirmed by motion.js:1101 ('by the element-holder KEY (a strokeId, or a meshId for an image mesh)', holderRefOf's own comment) and by meshHolder() (motion.js:4747-4750, `return ld.elementMotion[meshId] || null;`) using the EXACT SAME `ld.elementMotion[...]` access elementHolder() (motion.js:2911, `return ld.elementMotion ? ld.elementMotion[strokeId] : null;`) uses for an ordinary per-shape holder. This scope's own mesh-aware `self` accessors (packet 2) build meaning on top of resolveHolderLayer's generic, mesh-unaware result by feeding `r.strokeId` (whatever string it is) to `SMImageMesh.get()` and letting a miss (a real strokeId that is not also a registered meshId) fall through to `null` — resolveHolderLayer itself never asks the question.

Every one of the twelve packet-3 alias functions, plus aliasPosterizeTime, has EXACTLY ONE call site in the entire codebase: its own single positional slot in evalExpressionFor's sandbox argument list (C20m, motion.js:2572-2591). This is a stronger and more uniform statement than the issue's own framing ('argument unit conversion... seconds<->frames rounding') suggests in isolation — these functions exist ONLY to be handed to `new Function(...)` under an AE-shaped public name; none is ever called as an ordinary JS function from application code.

The AE alias table (packet 3's own responsibility field transcribes it verbatim by position) contains two genuine semantic gaps versus real After Effects behavior, neither previously flagged: (1) `sourceRectAtTime(t)` is bound directly to exprContentBox — a ZERO-ARGUMENT function (motion.js:2257) — so any `t` argument passed by a pasted AE snippet is silently discarded; the alias always returns the box of whatever frame is CURRENTLY being evaluated (exprContentBox's own comment at motion.js:2251-2256 states this scope honestly, but the alias binding does not warn a caller who expects AE's own per-time sampling). (2) `lookAt` is bound to exprAngleTo (motion.js:1693, pre-C20k), a 2D function returning a single DEGREES value (`Math.atan2(...)*180/Math.PI`) — a reasonable 2D substitute, but not AE's own lookAt(), which returns a 3-component 3D orientation vector for a 3D layer's Orient Rotation; a snippet written for a 3D AE rig that destructures lookAt's return as `[rx,ry,rz]` will silently receive a bare number instead.

`numKeys` is the only sandbox binding evaluated EAGERLY, at compile-of-argument-list time, rather than passed as a callable/getter: `exprNumKeys(holder, prop)` (C20k, motion.js:2070) is invoked once inline in the fn() call (motion.js:2583) and its RESULT — a plain number — is what the compiled expression sees bound to the name `numKeys`. Every other name in the same argument list (including this scope's own eleven alias functions) is a function reference the compiled code calls itself. Contrast self.keys.count (packet 1, SELF_VIEW.keys.count, an ES5 getter on SELF_KEYS) which IS re-evaluated live on every read within the same expression body.

`key`/`nearestKey` (the bare AE alias names) do not delegate to SELF_KEYS.at/nearest (packet 1) — aliasKey (motion.js:2294) and SELF_KEYS.at (motion.js:2173) are two independent one-line bodies with IDENTICAL logic (`exprKeyAt(c.holder, c.prop, Math.floor(_num(i)))`), not a shared helper. aliasNearestKey (motion.js:2290-2293) additionally converts its own argument from SECONDS to frames (`_num(t) * c.fps`) before calling exprNearestKeyAtFrame, while SELF_KEYS.nearest (motion.js:2174) takes frames directly with no conversion — the two sibling names speak different units on the SAME underlying built-in, which is the entire reason the compatibility-alias block exists (packet 3's own lead-in comment, motion.js:2277-2279, states this explicitly for the alias family as a whole).

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.matrix: a plain layer holder, a per-shape element holder (ld.elementMotion[strokeId]), a mesh-vertex holder (ld.elementMotion[meshId] for an attached image mesh), a detached/orphaned holder object not present in state.layers or any elementMotion map
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected: resolveHolderLayer returns {ld,index,strokeId:null} for the layer case and {ld,index,strokeId:<key>} identically for BOTH the per-shape and the mesh case (same branch, see boundaries); returns null for the detached holder; _selfResolved caches the result (including a null result) on ctx._resolved for the remainder of one evaluation, verified by counting resolveHolderLayer invocations across multiple self.* reads in a single expression body.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.matrix: self.isMesh/vertexIndex/vertexCount/vertexUV/isOutlineVertex/isShape evaluated on a plain layer holder, a per-shape shape holder, and a real mesh holder with prop='vtx3' on an 8-vertex mesh
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected: Non-mesh holders: isMesh=false, vertexIndex=-1, vertexCount=0, vertexUV=[0,0], isOutlineVertex=false, isShape=true only for the per-shape holder. Mesh holder: isMesh=true, vertexIndex=3, vertexCount=8, vertexUV=mesh.verts[3] (0..1 pair), isOutlineVertex=true only if index 3 is within mesh.outline.length, isShape=false regardless of strokeId being non-null.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.matrix: a per-shape holder with a live Paper item present, a per-shape holder whose item is momentarily absent (mid-rebuild), a whole-layer holder with no strokeId, a holder that resolves to nothing (window.userLayers absent or index out of range)
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected: Per-shape success returns the live item's own .bounds; the shape-absent case falls back to the whole layer's own bounds (userLayers[index].bounds); the unresolved case returns the all-zero {x:0,y:0,width:0,height:0,top:0,left:0} shape; top/left always exactly equal y/x in every non-zero case.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.matrix: valueAtTime(t)/velocityAtTime(t)/speedAtTime(t)/nearestKey(t) at a chosen seconds value t, crossed against self.at(f)/self.velocity(f)/self.speed(f)/self.keys.nearest(f) at f=t*fps on the SAME property/frame; key(i) crossed against self.keys.at(i); posterizeTime(n) crossed against a manual stepTime(fps/n) call; seedRandom(seed,true) crossed against seed(seed) followed by a manual rngTimeless flag read

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected: Both calls return the IDENTICAL box — the box of whatever frame is CURRENTLY being evaluated — confirming the alias silently discards its own time argument rather than sampling geometry at another frame, per the boundaries finding.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.matrix: lookAt(fromPoint, toPoint) on a 2D layer vs a 3D-enabled layer, with a snippet that destructures the result as an array
